correctness.rationale: The repaired Finding retains the arbitrary-center formula and strict barycentric comparison. The affine reduction gives the unhalved max/min cross-ratio. The exponential direction is uniform by the total-mass Jacobian; the scaled independent exponentials have rates x_i, and the minimum density calculation gives e^{-s}(P+P'/c) for the product P. Both boundary terms vanish in the integration by parts, giving the integral and subset sum. Strict Karamata applies for every positive s and strict majorization comparison. The small-radius coefficient follows by dominated convergence against e^{-s}s^n, with c~r. Independently, for two vertices the odds bounds give the interval length (1+c)x_1/(1+cx_1)-x_1/(1+cx_2), which agrees by expanding the subset sum. The frozen central formula and Gumbel limit are also mathematically consistent: use the beta recurrence and exponential max/log(n)->1 and scaled minimum Exp(1), without assuming their independence. Read the packaged checker and verification notes without executing the uploaded code; the all-dimension check is analytic.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-center law computes uniform Euclidean coverage for a given intrinsic neighborhood, including off-center candidates and local mass asymptotics. Strict barycentric majorization compares many nonoptimal centers at all radii, which a centroid optimum or its limiting quantile does not do. These are useful in their own right without reclaiming the earlier central results.
